title: Quantifying & Killing the AI Slop Fingerprint (240-Reply Study)
description: 240-reply OpenRouter study scoring AI slop across 8 models (Gemini 4 Neon, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Llama 4, Claude, GPT-6.2) & testing 4 anti-slop prompts.
h1: Measuring & killing the AI slop fingerprint across 8 frontier and open-weight models.
dek: 240 blind-evaluated writing tasks measure deterministic slop markers per 100 words alongside human-voice and clarity ratings—and prove a hybrid anti-slop prompt cuts markers from 1.23 to 0.10.
lede: Most advice on removing "AI-sounding writing" relies on personal pet-peeve word lists (banning delve or testament). Across 240 controlled writing replies (8 models on 10 everyday prompts plus a 4-model × 4-intervention shootout, spend $2.59), zero-lexicon cliche hits were no longer the main culprit on top frontier models—structural habits like em-dashes, prefatory framing ("Here is a ~140-word..."), and formulaic AI cadence drove ratings. While untuned defaults averaged 1.23 slop markers/100w (SD 3.95) and 30.0% blind-judged AI cadence, a Hybrid Anti-Slop Contract combining concrete structural bans with plainspoken voice cut slop markers to 0.10/100w (SD 0.44), dropped AI cadence from 30.0% to 0.0% [0.0–8.8%], eliminated em-dashes (0.38 → 0.00), and lifted blind human-voice score from 3.88 to 4.85/5 at top clarity (4.97/5).
answer: Banning isolated vocabulary clichés ('delve') alone misses modern AI slop: 0.00 lexicon hits appeared per default reply across all 7 top models except Llama 4 Maverick (0.60), yet blind judges flagged 30.0%–100.0% AI cadence on Gemini 4 Neon, DeepSeek V4 Pro, and Llama 4 Maverick. Use a Hybrid Anti-Slop prompt pairing explicit structural bans (zero em-dashes, zero sycophantic closers, zero 'Here is...' wrappers) with natural rhythm cues—cutting slop to 0.10/100w (SD 0.44), AI cadence to 0.0%, and raising clarity to 4.97/5.

sections.html:
Agents drafting emails, memos, docs, or editorial system prompts can apply this verified anti-slop policy directly (also in november-2026-agent-research-briefs.json):

Agent Decision Contract (YAML — expand to copy)
study_id: ai_slop_fingerprint
sample_size: 240 # 8 models x 10 default tasks (n=80 baseline) + 4 core models x 4 interventions x 10 tasks (n=160 intervention)
models_baseline_8: [openai/gpt-6.2-sol, anthropic/claude-fable-5-2, anthropic/claude-opus-5-5, openai/gpt-6.2-astra, x-ai/grok-4.7, meta-llama/llama-4-maverick, deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro, google/gemini-4-neon]
judge_model: google/gemini-4-argon
spend_usd: 2.5888
data_urls:
  briefs_json: https://agent-tune.com/research/data/november-2026-agent-research-briefs.json
  results_json: https://agent-tune.com/research/data/november-2026-ai-slop-fingerprint-results.json
  summary_csv: https://agent-tune.com/research/data/november-2026-ai-slop-fingerprint-summary.csv
if_then_decision_rules:
  - if: user asks to 'stop sounding like ChatGPT / AI' in emails, memos, or docs
    then: apply hybrid_anti_slop (slop 1.23 -> 0.10/100w, AI cadence 30.0% -> 0.0%, human 4.85/5, clarity 4.97/5, 0.00 em-dashes)
  - if: model is Llama 4 Maverick, DeepSeek V4 Pro, or Gemini 4 Neon
    then: treat structural anti-slop rules as mandatory (baselines hit 100.0%, 70.0%, and 50.0% AI cadence)
anti_patterns:
  - Relying solely on a banned-word list ('delve', 'tapestry'): misses synthetic symmetry, meta-wrappers, and rhythm ticks.
  - Overly tight sentence-rhythm rules alone without clarity anchors: clipped early replies weighed down rhythm_rubric clarity (4.53/5 vs 4.97/5 hybrid).
recommended_prompt_recipe: |
  Write like a crisp, thoughtful practitioner—never a template or hype brochure.
  Start cleanly in the deliverable itself with zero meta-intros ('Here is...') or helpful sign-offs.
  Ban em-dashes, 'not just X, it's Y' contrasts, bolded bullet lists, and stock clichés ('delve', 'testament', 'thrilled').
  Vary sentence length naturally and ground claims in specific verbs and concrete facts.
scope_limits: Deterministic regex marker counts paired with single blind judge (Gemini 4 Argon) across 10 short-form business writing tasks (~115-135 words).

Notice the trade-off across interventions: plainspoken_persona felt warmest (4.92/5), yet kept emitting em-dashes (0.42/reply vs 0.00), leaving DeepSeek at 20.0% AI cadence. Meanwhile, hybrid_anti_slop reached 0.0% AI cadence on every model (0.00 slop on Claude Fable 5.2 and DeepSeek V4 Pro) and the highest clarity (4.97/5).

Real verbatim outputs on identical prompts show why structural tell-removal beats simple cliché word bans:

  • Llama 4 Maverick Baseline (launch_email · Human 1/5 · AI Cadence True): Opened with template meta-chatter and fake enthusiasm: "Here is a ~140-word product launch email: Subject: Exciting Updates: v2.0 is Live! Dear valued beta users, We're thrilled to announce the launch of v2.0, packed with features you've been asking for!..."
  • Gemini 4 Neon Baseline vs. Hybrid Anti-Slop (launch_email):
    • Default (AI Cadence True, 3/5 human): "Hi [Name], Thanks to your incredible feedback during our beta, we’re thrilled to announce that Version 2.0 is officially live! You asked, we listened..."
    • Hybrid Anti-Slop (AI Cadence False, 5/5 human, 5/5 clarity, 0.00 slop): "Subject: Version 2.0 is live: fast CSV imports and dark mode. Version 2.0 is ready in your account right now. You asked for faster data uploads and a break from the bright white screen during late-night sessions. We built both. Our new CSV importer handles 50,000 rows in under four seconds..."

Scope & Limitations: Regex slop density, em-dash counts, and sycophantic closures were scored deterministically; human-likeness, clarity, and AI cadence ratings came from a single blind judge (google/gemini-4-argon). Sample size is n = 10 replies per model in the 8-model leaderboard (wider CIs) and n = 40 per intervention arm across 4 models. Notice also 5 brief generation truncations under strict rhythm_rubric (12–23 words) dragged its pooled clarity to 4.53/5, reinforcing why combining positive voice structure with targeted bans (hybrid_anti_slop) performed best.

faq.q: Which AI models produce the most AI slop by default?
faq.a: Across 10 workplace writing prompts per model, untuned Llama 4 Maverick (100.0% blind-judged AI cadence, 1.80/5 human score), DeepSeek V4 Pro (70.0% AI cadence, 1.07 slop/100w), and Gemini 4 Neon (50.0% AI cadence, 3.41 slop/100w including one 4-word em-dash outlier; 1.01 trimmed) showed the strongest synthetic tells, while GPT-6.2 Sol, GPT-6.2 Astra, and Claude Fable 5.2 hit 0.0% AI cadence.

faq.q: Do banned-word lists like 'never say delve' remove AI slop?
faq.a: Only partially. Banning words alone scored 0.21 slop markers/100w and 4.50/5 human-voice score, because modern models rarely say 'delve' unprompted anymore—the real tells are em-dashes, 'Here is a...' wrappers, fake enthusiasm, and symmetrical phrasing. Combining structural bans with plainspoken cadence (Hybrid Anti-Slop) cut AI cadence to 0.0% and hit 4.97/5 clarity.
